title: Systematic Localization of Late-Time Cosmological Signals in Modified Gravity: CMB Survival, the Lensing Barrier, and a Growth-Sector Sign Constraint
description: Five-phase localization study of where late-time modified-gravity signals can reside, using Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) as a case study. The background gate collapses (alpha consistent with zero) under joint CMB+BAO+SNe, pure growth modification (mu<1 with Sigma=1) is blocked by CMB lensing, and a narrow perturbation-sector slip window survives Planck with mu≈0.94 and Sigma≈1.05. The surviving valley is degenerate with the Planck AL anomaly, but fσ8 growth data independently favor mu<1, providing a growth-sector sign constraint.

efc_friedmann.description: EFC late-time background modification to the Friedmann equation via an additive gate of strength α.

logistic_gate.description: Logistic gate activating near scale factor a_t with width δ_a, confining modifications to late times.

mu_parametrization.description: Modified Poisson equation for the Newtonian potential; µ encodes effective clustering strength (growth coupling).

sigma_parametrization.description: Modification to the lensing potential; Σ directly controls CMB and galaxy-lensing deflections.

gravitational_slip.description: Gravitational slip parameter; η ≠ 1 requires two independent metric potentials and implies anisotropic stress.

key_results.main_finding: The background channel is observationally empty (α → 0), pure growth-modification is excluded by the CMB lensing barrier, and a narrow perturbation-sector slip window survives Planck at (µ≈0.94, Σ≈1.05), degenerate with AL but supported in sign by fσ8.

sealed_predictions.statement: Future joint CMB lensing + RSD analyses will prefer a weakened-growth, enhanced-lensing slip regime with µ < 1 and Σ > 1 (approximately µ ∈ [0.93, 0.96], Σ ∈ [1.03, 1.07]) yielding η > 1 at late times.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Simultaneous constraints from Stage-III/IV CMB lensing reconstructions (ACT/SPT/SO/Planck-legacy) and DESI/Euclid RSD that find µ ≥ 1 or Σ ≤ 1 at >3σ over 0.3 < z < 1.5.

sealed_predictions.statement: The growth-sector sign constraint will persist: fσ8 measurements will continue to prefer suppressed growth relative to GR (consistent with µ < 1) at z ≈ 0.3–1.0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI full-shape RSD and Euclid Year-1/Year-3 reporting fσ8 consistent with GR to ≲2% precision and excluding µ < 0.96 at >3σ across 0.3 < z < 1.2.

kill_criteria: KC1: Joint Planck/ACT/SPT/SO CMB lensing + TTTEEE + ISW constraints that exclude the slip window µ ∈ [0.93, 0.96] and Σ ∈ [1.03, 1.07] at >3σ after profiling over ΛCDM parameters.
KC2: DESI full-shape RSD and Euclid growth-rate measurements consistent with GR (µ = 1) to ≲2% over 0.3 < z < 1.2, excluding µ < 0.96 at >3σ.
KC3: High-precision CMB lensing reconstructions yield Σ = 1.00 ± 0.01 at z ~ 1 scales (modes contributing to Cℓ^{ϕϕ}), excluding Σ > 1.03 at >3σ when marginalizing over µ.

KC4: Robust resolution of the Planck AL anomaly to AL → 1 by improved beam/calibration and cross-experiments, combined with RSD consistent with GR, such that the (µ≈0.94, Σ≈1.05) configuration worsens the full CMB likelihood by Δχ² > +5 relative to GR.

KC5: Late-time relativistic probes of anisotropic stress (e.g., relativistic galaxy-bispectrum or lensing–ISW cross) constrain gravitational slip to η = 1.00 ± 0.02 for 0.3 < z < 1.0 and k ~ 0.05–0.2 h Mpc⁻¹, excluding η ≳ 1.08 at >3σ.
abstract_short: Five-phase localization study testing EFC against Planck 2018 CMB, DESI 2024 BAO, SDSS DR12 BAO, and Pantheon+ SNe. Background sector is observationally empty (α → 0 under joint constraints). Perturbation sector survives Planck within a narrow slip window (μ ∈ [0.93, 0.96], Σ ∈ [1.03, 1.07]). The (μ, Σ) valley is degenerate with the A_L anomaly (cos = 0.93), but fσ₈ data independently confirm μ < 1 at > 2σ, breaking the degeneracy.

alpha_background.description: Best-fit background coupling (joint Planck+DESI+Pantheon+). Consistent with zero.

eta_slip.description: Gravitational slip η = Σ/μ ≈ 1.05/0.94 at sweet spot

sigma_lensing_fit.description: Parabolic fit to lensing likelihood at μ = 0.94

corr_alpha_H0.description: Near-perfect degeneracy between α and H₀ in Planck-only fit

growth_rate.description: Growth-rate data for B0 bridge test

phase1_background.conclusion: No dataset combination exceeds 2σ. Background gate is observationally empty.

phase3_AL_degeneracy.conclusion: The (μ, Σ) valley is the A_L anomaly expressed through physical metric potentials.

phase4_growth_sign.sign_constraint: μ < 1 (weakened gravity) at > 2σ, independent of A_L
phase4_growth_sign.relevant_scales: k ≈ 0.05–0.1 h/Mpc (original k_Λ = 0.0014 h/Mpc has zero effect)

incompatibilities.detail: Grid-AQUAL gives μ_GRAV > 1, CMB+fσ₈ require μ < 1
Single potential implies Φ = Ψ (η = 1), CMB requires η ≈ 1.12
At k_Λ = 0.0014 h/Mpc, modification < 0.1% at k > 0.01 h/Mpc

phase5_theory_gap.requirement: Relativistic EFC perturbation theory with two independent metric potentials, μ < 1, Σ > 1

surviving_signal_spec.lensing: Σ ≈ 1.05; gravitational slip η ≠ 1 is essential

key_conclusions: EFC background sector is observationally empty: α → 0 under joint CMB+BAO+SNe constraints
Pure growth-modification (μ < 1, Σ = 1) is excluded by CMB lensing
A narrow μ–Σ degeneracy valley survives Planck at (μ ≈ 0.94, Σ ≈ 1.05) with Δχ² = −0.45
The (μ, Σ) valley is degenerate with the Planck A_L anomaly (cos = 0.93)
fσ₈ data independently confirm μ < 1 at > 2σ, breaking the A_L degeneracy
A relativistic EFC perturbation theory producing gravitational slip is required
Results are largely model-independent and applicable to any late-time MG framework
